messages:
maria: Heads-up — on the new private deploy we just toggled RBAC to restrict controller-manager. After the change I'm seeing a gap in audit logs for KMS crypto operations. Not sure if it's a side effect of the permission delta or the logging agent crashing. anyone seen this?
ken: Hmm. Did the change remove the ServiceAccount that allowed the logging-daemonset to read /var/log/journal ?
jordan: @maria can you paste the exact RBAC diff? quick check: if the logging SA lost access to secrets/keys it might drop key IDs in logs but still log events.
maria: here's the minimal diff we applied:

```yaml
- kind: ClusterRoleBinding
  name: controller-manager:access
  subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: controller-manager
    namespace: kube-system
+ kind: ClusterRoleBinding
  name: controller-manager:access
  subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: controller-manager
    namespace: kube-system
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: kms-proxy
    namespace: infra
```

maria: we added kms-proxy into the binding, not removed anything. logging-daemonset still has its SA.
nilesh: odd. Could be unrelated — we upgraded the kms-proxy sidecar yesterday which switched from writing audit events to stdout to sending them over TLS to our SIEM. Did the TLS handshake fail? check the proxy logs.
security-bot: deploy-event: rollout/kms-proxy v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0 rolled at 3778878000. health: degraded -> recovered (see deploy-bot).
deploy-bot: rollout failed at step 3 for 2 minutes due to liveness probe flakes, then retried and succeeded.
ken: If the sidecar temporarily failed, logs might have been buffered locally and then dropped if disk pressure happened. Check node free space and container restart counts.
jordan: Also verify the audit policy in kube-apiserver. If the policy changed to omit authorization decision or to filter sensitive fields, KMS events could be suppressed.
maria: kube-apiserver flags are unchanged per our bootstrap (verified). Node disks look fine too. kms-proxy logs show repeated TLS: certificate verify failed
nilesh: Ah — certificate rotation for internal CA happened last night during the keyroll. The proxy wasn't updated with the new CA bundle. That would cause handshake errors and no events shipped.
ken: Two follow-ups: 1) restore audit coverage for the window (we need local copies), 2) harden so this can't silently drop data in future.
jordan: For (1) — check /var/log/kms-proxy/* and /var/log/pods/* on nodes that had the sidecar. We might have archived chunks. If logs were lost, we must mark an incident and escalate to customers per SLA.
maria: copying from a node now. if we find holes we'll open an incident and notify affected tenants.
nilesh: For (2) — proposal: require an egress allowlist and enforced TLS pinning for KMS endpoints, plus persistent disk quota for logging buffers. Also add an event-level test in our CI that simulates KMS handshake failure and asserts no silent drops.
ken: Agreed. I'd add: network policy that denies outbound to internet from infra namespace, only allow to internal KMS IPs via an egress proxy. Also add an admission webhook that prevents rolling out KMS-related changes without a canary in a staging VPC.
jordan: We should also ensure audit logs are written to an append-only object store (encrypted) as a second sink. If sidecar fails, we still have the local journald + archive shipper process.
maria: Sounds good. Quick netpol snippet for infra namespace egress deny (testable):

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: infra-egress-lockdown
  namespace: infra
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.20.0/24 # KMS cluster
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

nilesh: We'll also add a dedicated bastion/jumpbox for any out-of-band KMS admin operations — no direct node SSH from developer IPs. Enforce MFA and short-lived certs.
ken: And RBAC: split the KMS proxy role into two roles — crypto-only (no audit config) and audit-sink-writer (only can write to logging bucket). That reduces blast radius when rotating permissions.
jordan: For incident response: create a one-page runbook: steps to identify TLS handshake failures, how to attach the correct CA to running pods (kubectl patch secret), steps to rehydrate logs to SIEM, and notification template for tenants.
maria: I'll draft the runbook. Can one of you own the CI test for simulated handshake failures? @nilesh?nilesh: I can take CI test. I'll add a job that spins up a tiny KMS mock that rejects TLS and assert our shipper retries and falls back to disk-first retention.
ken: I'll implement the RBAC split and netpol in a canary namespace and run through the runbook with you @maria.
security-bot: incident-note: possible partial audit gap detected 3778879000-3778880500. severity: medium. owners: @maria @ken @nilesh.
maria: thanks. i'll open the incident and post updates here. low-bandwidth timeline: 1) find logs 2) confirm gap 3) notify customers if gap > 5m 4) ship CI + netpol + RBAC split 5) postmortem.
maria: update 1 — found archived logs on node-07: /var/log/kms-proxy/archived/2026-03-21T03:10Z.tar.gz. extracting now.
jordan: nice. keep the thread updated and flag any customer-facing text for review before we send.
maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
